samples.summary: Scope creep past the task plan: an API-key authority/revocation overhaul rides along with the class-A′ close
samples.evidence: The originating plan (docs/tasks/active/20260903-api-v1-folders-copy-todo.md, "Plan → Backend") asks for a v1 folders controller, a copy route, a `folderId` on the document PATCH, and specs; "Out of scope" names only classes B and C. This diff additionally (a) makes `WorkspaceScopeGuard` run `assertMember` for *every* API-key request on *every* existing v1 route (workspace-scope.guard.ts:40), (b) rewrites `WorkspaceService.removeMember` into an interactive transaction that revokes `apiKey` rows (workspace.service.ts:109-123), and (c) adds a membership check to `ApiV1ImageReadController.assertCanRead` (image-read.controller.ts:95). None of these are folders/copy/move: they change the semantics of already-shipped endpoints (`DELETE /api/v1/.../documents/:did` previously granted a write-scoped key workspace authority — backend.md's old text — and now refuses a key whose minter is not a manager), add a write to a table this service did not own, and add a DB round-trip to every API-key request. The plan's "resolved against that user's membership at request time" bullet covers the *new* routes' gating; the cross-cutting guard change, the revocation-on-removal path and the image-read change are extra surface a reviewer of "close A′" is not expecting. It is documented (rest-api.md §5.8, backend.md), so the cost is scope, not breakage.

samples.summary: Controller-level folder/document authorization + move validation is duplicated rather than shared with the web controllers
samples.evidence: `ApiV1FoldersController.isManager` (folders.controller.ts:78-89) and its `update` body assembly (:114-142) are a near-line-for-line copy of `FolderController.resolveFolderManager` (folder/folder.controller.ts:30-39) and `FolderController.update` (:74-104), down to the `assertSameWorkspace` → `assertNoCycle` → `update` ordering and the ForbiddenException wording. The same holds for `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` (api/v1/documents.controller.ts:122-150) versus `DocumentController.updateDocument` (document/document.controller.ts:310-345). Reuse here stopped at `FolderService` and `isDocumentManager`; the *gate* — the part whose divergence changes who may move what via CLI versus browser — was copied. A shared helper (e.g. on FolderService, or the existing `document-access` module) would keep one answer to "who may move this".

samples.summary: WorkspaceService reaches directly into `apiKey` rows, bypassing ApiKeyService which owns revocation
samples.evidence: `removeMember` now issues `tx.apiKey.updateMany({ ... data: { revokedAt: new Date() } })`. Key revocation already lives in `packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.service.ts:61` (`data: { revokedAt: new Date() }`), and the api-key module owns the `revokedAt` invariant checked at validation time (:76). Putting a second writer of that column in the workspace service means the revocation rule is now expressed in two layers; the atomicity requirement could be met by passing the transaction client to an ApiKeyService method instead.

samples.summary: New `folderId` on the v1 document PATCH uses an inline body type while the sibling folders controller (and the web route) reuse validated DTOs
samples.evidence: `update(@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null })` — no DTO, so no `@IsUUID()`/`@Length` validation, while the new `ApiV1FoldersController` in the same change correctly reuses `CreateFolderDto`/`UpdateFolderDto` (folder/folder.dto.ts) and the web equivalent uses `UpdateDocumentDto` (document/document.controller.ts:314). The existing v1 `create` handler is inline too, so this follows local precedent rather than the reuse the same PR demonstrates one file over; the mismatch is why the null-vs-undefined semantics have to be re-explained in prose in three docs.

samples.summary: The task plan for this work ships with every checkbox unticked and the Review section empty
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260903-api-v1-folders-copy-todo.md lists the whole Plan (Backend / CLI / Docs, lines 41-80) as `[ ]` and ends with "## Review — _To be filled in when the work lands._", even though the sibling todo (20260831-agentic-office-workflow-todo.md:70-80) already marks step 4 closed and points at this file. CONTRIBUTING.md:62-76 makes the per-task plan the record of the work, so the bookkeeping half of the plan's own Docs checklist is the one item left undone. (The other doc targets — cli.md, rest-api.md, workspace-folders.md, agentic-office-workflow.md, packages/cli/README.md:118-123 and packages/backend/README.md:626-629 — are all updated.)

samples.summary: Per-document gating for API keys sits near rest-api.md's "no granular per-document permission scoping on API keys" non-goal
samples.evidence: rest-api.md Non-Goals still reads "Granular per-document or per-cell permission scoping on API keys (may be added later)", while this change makes an API key's ability to move/delete a specific document depend on that document's `authorID` via `isDocumentManager`. It is a restriction derived from the minter's role rather than a per-key scope, so I read it as compatible — but the non-goal now needs the reader to make that distinction unaided.

finding.summary: The new "a key's authority dies with its minter's membership" invariant is implemented twice and the two copies now disagree; the docs claim it holds for the whole v1 surface
finding.evidence: `WorkspaceScopeGuard` (workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-38) now requires `assertMember(resolvedId, user.id)` for API-key callers. `ApiV1ImageReadController` does not mount that guard (`@UseGuards(OptionalCombinedAuthGuard)`, image-read.controller.ts:41) and re-implements the check locally: `if (user?.isApiKey) { if (user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId) return; ... }` — scope match only, no membership. So the same question ("may this key act in this workspace?") gets two different answers, and the delta's own doc text is wrong: docs/design/rest-api.md:517-519 says "`WorkspaceScopeGuard` enforces the removal half for the **whole** v1 surface", and folders.controller.ts:68-74 / backend.md:293-297 make the same unqualified claim. A key whose minter was removed keeps reading every workspace image.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence is not in the repository. image-read.controller.ts:97-113 performs BOTH the scope match and `await this.workspaceService.assertMember(resolvedWorkspaceId, Number(user.id))` for API-key callers — identical to WorkspaceScopeGuard's pair at workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-45. The reviewer's snippet ("`if (user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId) return;` — scope match only, no membership") does not exist; the only `return` is at line 112, after assertMember. So the two copies do NOT disagree and the claimed consequence ("a key whose minter was removed keeps reading every workspace image") is unreachable — such a key is refused at line 108. The doc misstatement is likewise not present: docs/design/rest-api.md:531-534 explicitly says "Every v1 controller mounts the guard except `ApiV1ImageReadController` ... it repeats the same scope + membership pair by hand (`assertCanRead`)"; the quoted phrase "for the whole v1 surface" appears nowhere in the repo. folders.controller.ts:64-75 documents only the folders `isManager` gate, and docs/design/backend.md:291-299 is scoped to the DELETE documents route (which does mount the guard at documents.controller.ts:29) — neither makes an unqualified whole-surface claim. What remains is a deliberate, documented two-line repetition over a shared service method (assertMember), which the guard's own docstring (workspace-scope.guard.ts:24-26) explains cannot be a mounted guard because the route also serves anonymous share-token viewers; that is at most a non-blocking minor reuse point, not the major divergence claimed.
